title: Conjecture on maximum cliques with no $K_t$-immersion
statement_text: The maximum number of cliques in a graph on $n \geq t-2$ vertices with no $K_t$-immersion is $2^{t-2}(n-t+3)$.
context_text: A weak $H$-immersion in $G$ is an injective map $\phi:V(H)\to V(G)$ together with pairwise edge-disjoint paths, one for each edge $uv$ of $H$, joining $\phi(u)$ and $\phi(v)$; it is strong if no internal vertex of these paths lies in $\phi(V(H))$, and if moreover the paths are internally vertex-disjoint it is an $H$-subdivision (topological minor). The number of cliques counts all complete subgraphs, including the empty one (as in the count below). The authors prove that for $t$ sufficiently large every $n$-vertex graph with no strong (hence no weak) $K_t$-immersion has at most $2^{t+\log_2^2t}n$ cliques, which is sharp up to a factor $2^{O(\log^2t)}$. The conjectured value comes from the following graph with no weak $K_t$-immersion: a clique $K$ on $t-2$ vertices plus $n-t+2$ further vertices each adjacent exactly to $K$; the outside vertices have degree less than $t-1$, while the $t$ branch vertices of a $K_t$-immersion need degree at least $t-1$, and the cliques are a subset of $K$ together with at most one outside vertex, giving $2^{t-2}(n-t+3)$ cliques. The conjecture is stated in prose for '$K_t$-immersion' without specifying weak or strong. For comparison, the maximum number of cliques is $3^{2t/3+o(t)}n$ for $K_t$-minor-free graphs.

title: Conjecture on optimal exponential constant for $K_t$-subdivision clique count
statement_text: The maximum number of cliques in an $n$-vertex graph with no $K_t$-subdivision is $3^{2t/3+o(t)}n$, i.e., the optimal exponential constant in the exponent is $\frac{2}{3}\log_2 3 \approx 1.06$.
context_text: A weak $H$-immersion in $G$ is an injective map $\phi:V(H)\to V(G)$ together with pairwise edge-disjoint paths, one for each edge $uv$ of $H$, joining $\phi(u)$ and $\phi(v)$; it is strong if no internal vertex of these paths lies in $\phi(V(H))$, and if moreover the paths are internally vertex-disjoint it is an $H$-subdivision (topological minor). The number of cliques counts all complete subgraphs, including the empty one (as in the count below). Norine, Seymour, Thomas and Wollan, and independently Reed and Wood, showed that $n$-vertex $K_t$-minor-free graphs have at most $c(t)n$ cliques; Lee and Oum proved $c(t)<c^t$ for an absolute constant $c$ (also for subdivisions), and the authors proved earlier that $c(t)=3^{2t/3+o(t)}$ for minors. Here they prove that every $n$-vertex graph with no $K_t$-subdivision has at most $2^{1.817t+o(t)}n$ cliques. Wood's lower-bound construction for minors also has no $K_t$-subdivision, so the constant $1.817$ cannot be improved below $\frac23\log_23\approx1.06$; the conjecture is that this constant is best possible, as for minors. Note that $n$-vertex graphs with no $K_t$-subdivision have $O(t^2n)$ edges (Komlós–Szemerédi, Bollobás–Thomason).
